routes.constraint: The selected application test function remains byte-identical.
routes.success: Documented public framework and runner APIs expose every registered and observed contract field without source parsing or app-authored success metadata.

routes.constraint: Application code exports only a bounded generator/predicate entrypoint; the adapter owns framework execution, parameters, result capture, and normalization.
routes.success: The driver emits a closed report that the adapter checks against registration, artifacts, inventory, and process provenance.

required_contract_fields: generator entrypoint and exact closure identity

attacks.mutation: replace the registered seed and retain the old report
replace the requested case budget with the same completed count
replace the generator entrypoint while retaining its outer label
change one generator-closure byte and refresh only the outer contract identity
substitute one target with a same-count target
omit or duplicate one structured report field
let source-local settings override the registered seed or budget
reinterpret a legacy contract digest as explicit sampling
change persistence from disabled to ambient writable database
change framework version while retaining framework name

decision.q1: Both frameworks preserve every required contract field and project to one backend-neutral constructor.
decision.q2: Every required observation is independently tied to registration and exact process/artifact provenance; all attacks fail with their registered class.
decision.q3: Select the least intrusive route that passes Q1 and Q2 without inferred fields. If only the driver ABI passes, record instrumentation as failed rather than averaging the routes.
decision.q4: Legacy and explicit records remain distinct versioned constructors and all migration attacks fail.
decision.unblock_exp_0005_q1_field_012: Q1, Q2, and Q4 pass in independent Rust and Python implementations.
